nodes.summary: Index the Fibonacci numbers as $F_1 = 1$, $F_2 = 2$, $F_{i+1} = F_i + F_{i-1}$. Let $n$ be such that the state consisting of $n$ copies of $F_1$ (the starting position of the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game on $n$) is losing. Then for every $k$ with $1 \le k \le 5$ and $3k \le n$, the state consisting of $k$ copies of $F_3$ and $n - 3k$ copies of $F_1$ is losing.

nodes.summary: Index the Fibonacci numbers as $F_1 = 1$, $F_2 = 2$, $F_{i+1} = F_i + F_{i-1}$. Let $n \ge 1$ and let $F_k$ be the largest Fibonacci number with $F_k \le n$, the largest term of the Zeckendorf decomposition of $n$. Then every complete Accelerated Zeckendorf Game on $n$ (a sequence of moves from $n$ copies of $F_1$ to a state from which no move is possible) has at least $k - 1$ moves.

nodes.summary: Index the Fibonacci numbers as $F_1 = 1$, $F_2 = 2$, $F_{i+1} = F_i + F_{i-1}$, and let $k \ge 1$. Every complete Accelerated Zeckendorf Game on $F_k$ (a sequence of moves from $F_k$ copies of $F_1$ to a state from which no move is possible) has at least $k - 1$ moves, and some complete game on $F_k$ has exactly $k - 1$ moves.
nodes.title: Sharp lower bound for the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game on a Fibonacci number

nodes.summary: Every state of the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game from which no move is possible is a losing state.
nodes.title: Terminal states are losing in the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game

nodes.summary: The losing and the winning states of the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game are defined by simultaneous induction: a state is losing when every move from it leads to a winning state, and a state is winning when some move from it leads to a losing state. In particular every state from which no move is possible is losing.

nodes.summary: For every $n$, if the state consisting of $n$ copies of $F_1$ is winning, then exactly one state reachable from it in one move is losing: when the first player has a winning strategy in the game on $n$, exactly one first move preserves it.

nodes.summary: The sequence whose states are all the empty state is a complete Accelerated Zeckendorf Game on $0$ with $0$ moves.
nodes.title: The complete game on $0$

nodes.summary: A sequence of states $g_0, g_1, \dots$ is a complete Accelerated Zeckendorf Game on $n$ with $L$ moves if $g_0$ consists of $n$ copies of $F_1$, for every $j < L$ some move takes $g_j$ to $g_{j+1}$, and no move is possible from $g_L$. The states after $g_L$ play no role.

nodes.title: The Zeckendorf state of $4$

nodes.title: The Zeckendorf state of zero is empty

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
